source_text: Quartum a lascivientibus perpetratur, id est, illius voluptatis excessus, et quia de insolentia, non de natura contingit iure damnatur Aut in coniugibus cum honestate exercetur, aut in castis virtute frenatur In coniugibus cum honestate exercetur
pass_a_gloss: Quartum from lascivientibus perpetratur, it is, of-that of-pleasure excessus, and because about/from insolentia, not about/from nature contingit by-right condemns or in spouses when/with honestate exercetur, or in castis by-virtue frenatur in spouses when/with honestate exercetur.

lemmas.lexica: LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself

pass_b_english: Sexual desire is interrupted by bodily weakness.
In married people it is exercised honorably; in those who abstain it is restrained by virtue.
The fourth thing—the excess of that pleasure—is committed by the sexually unrestrained. Since it arises from recklessness, not from nature, it is rightly condemned.

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
